previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with type 1 diabetes, hypertension, and a history of depression and alcohol use in remission, was admitted with diabetic ketoacidosis due to insulin noncompliance, likely exacerbated by stress from caring for her ill mother. She presented with nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, polyuria, and a blood glucose over 500. She was treated in the MICU with IV fluids and an insulin drip, which resolved the DKA. A central line was placed for reliable access. Her renal function, initially impaired due to prerenal azotemia, normalized with hydration. A nonproductive cough was evaluated with a chest X-ray showing no pneumonia and was managed conservatively. Her insulin regimen was transitioned to glargine at bedtime with a sliding scale of lispro, and she received diabetes education. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged for diabetes management and social support.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ woman with Type 1 dibetes and history of alcohol abuse 
admitted with generalized malaise, nausea and vomiting found to 
have diabetic ketoacidosis and acute kidney injury, initially 
admitted to the ICU. 

# DKA: Patient presented similar to prior admissions with 
profound hyperglycemia, large anion gap acidosis, ketones in 
urine and elevated lactate. Etiology most likely poor adherence 
at home (was not taking insulin for 2 days), and possible URI as 
contributor. Her infectious work up was negative including blood 
and urine cultures and CXR.  She was started on an insulin drip 
and received aggressive IVF (total 9L in the ICU, currently 7L 
positive LOS). ___ was consulted and she was quickly able to 
be transitioned to long acting insulin with humalog sliding 
scale, and was off of the insulin drip by 9pm on the day of 
admission, tolerating PO well. She is currently doing well on 
her home 36 glargine with sliding scale, with all FSG in past 24 
hours 100-180s, though did have an episode of asymptomatic 
hypoglycemia on the morning of transfer to ___, resolved 
quickly after glucose paste. 

# Acute kidney injury: Due to volume depletion on admission in 
setting of profound hyperglycemia and osmotic diuresis as well 
as poor PO intake. Hyperkalemia and creatinine normalized 
quickly on admission with aggressive hydration. 

# Iron Deficiency Anemia: found to have Iron of 10 and Ferritin 
of 12. No signs of overt bleeding. Started daily ferrous sulfate 
with bowel regimen. 

# EtOH Abuse: No signs of withdrawal this admission. Did not 
require benzodiazepines or phenbarbital in the ICU. Started on 
thiamine, folate, and multivitamin. 

# Rhinorrhea: patient believes this is her seasonal allergies, 
though could reflect URI. Started loratidine per patient 
request.
